settings.description: How long a database operation waits for a lock held by another process before it fails.
How long acknowledged mail is kept before it is deleted. Pending mail is never deleted.
How long activity records are kept before cleanup deletes them.
The most activity records the store keeps. When it is exceeded, cleanup deletes the oldest records first, whatever their age.
Refused requests with the same outcome write at most one activity record per window; the next record says how many were left out. Zero records every refusal.
How often the service deletes mail and activity that are past their retention. The service reads it once, at start.
The disk budget for all managed state of the store.
The share of the disk budget at which health reports a warning.

The share of the disk budget at which send is refused with storage_full. Reading, acknowledging, waiting, cleanup and every owner operation keep working. Set it above storage.warning_percent so the warning comes first.
How long delivered mail may stay unacknowledged before it is reported as overdue.
The default and maximum time a wait for new mail may stay parked. Zero disables parked waits.
The largest subject of a message, in UTF-8 bytes.
The largest body of a message, in UTF-8 bytes.
The most messages one inbox page returns.
The most distinct recipients one message may have.
The most pending deliveries one principal may have. A send that would pass it is refused; nothing is deleted to make room.
The most waits the service keeps parked at once. Zero admits none.
The most waits one principal may keep parked at once. Zero admits none.
The most connections the service keeps open at once. A connection past it is closed without an answer. The service reads it once, at start.

The connections kept for the owner. Agent requests, parked waits included, are refused with too_many_connections once agents hold limits.connections minus this reserve. At least one connection stays open to agents. The service reads it once, at start.
How long a client has to send its whole request. A slower client is closed. The service reads it once, at start.
The largest request or response frame on the service socket. A larger frame is refused before its body is read.
